newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CEURO MKTS UP, HIGHS FOR PRAGUE, WARSAW, BRATISLAVA.
newsitem.headline: CEURO MKTS UP, HIGHS FOR PRAGUE, WARSAW, BRATISLAVA.

text.p: Share prices on central and
east European bourses moved upwards across-the-board this week,
reaching highs in Prague, Warsaw and Bratislava.
The Central European Share Index (CESI), which reflects
price movements in 73 Polish, Czech, Hungarian, Slovak and
Slovenian stocks, edged higher over the week to close at a new
record high of 1,726.32 points.
PRAGUE
Spectacular gains to the PX50's biggest banking issue,
Komercni Banka, spurred the index on to a new 12-month high of
613.4 on Thursday with dealers seeing further advances in the
coming sessions.
Komercni, which has risen nearly 10 percent since the
beginning of the week, was pushed by strong long term arbitrage
possibilities existing between Komercni's price on the Prague
bourse, 2,905 at Thursday's close, and its global depositary
receipt price in London, currently 3,446.
"It is definitely not normal. There's clear arbitrage
opportunity - although this cannot be realised at the moment,"
sad Lubomir Vystavel of ING Barings.
WARSAW
The Warsaw Stock Exchange edged up 0.2 percent this week,
setting a 35-month high on Tuesday, but analysts expected it to
fall in profit-taking next week after having gained about 38
percent since mid-December.
"All ratios of technical analysis are overheated and show
sell-signals, companies earnings reports for January were not
spectacular, so surely the correction will happen," said Pawel
Dmytryk, a trader at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
Some analysts said the expected profit-taking correction
could last about a month but they added that Poland's good
economic prospects and expanding possibilities such as new
issues and forthcoming large privatisations were attracting
new, foreign capital, which could later push the WIG index up.
BUDAPEST
Hungarian share prices edged a shade higher through the
week as bourse-listed companies completed the publication of
their preliminary 1996 earnings reports. On Thursday the BUX
index finished at 5,578.73 points, up 58.33 from last Friday.
"The market reached the end of an expansive period and
investors will now review what to invest in," one trader said.
The share market has calmed down and another reason was
that investors were waiting for the planned new phase of a
selloff in oil company MOL.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) extended last week's
uptrend with four consecutive year highs this week, and brokers
said the increase may continue further due to strong demand for
still undervalued blue chips and high interbank market rates
prompting foreign capital to turn to stock market.
The 16-share SAX index rose 5.28 points, or 2.68 percent,
to close at 201.95 points on Thursday from Monday's open.
"In principle, blue chips are rising, and trading has
become more lively as currently higher interbank money market
rates had attracted some foreign capital inflow," Vladimir
Kuklis, a CSOB Bank analyst said. "It appears that the trend
will continue for a while."
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks were mixed in slower trade on Thursday
after recovering most of the lost ground earlier in the week,
and market participants foresaw stagnation unless foreign
investors step in to prop up trade.
"It is hard to say what any of the big buyers are up to,"
said Marko Nikolac at Metroholding brokerage.
He singled out Kras chocolate maker, gaining 15 kuna this
week on relatively large volumes, as having good prospects.
The company said it was near closing an investment deal
with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares rose 2.5 percent by Thursday close, as the
blue-chip SBI index increased 34.7 points to 1,404.1.
Pharmaceuticals trader Salus outperformed the market, rising
14.9 percent, while financial consultancy Primofin bucked the
trend, plummeting 13 percent.
BUCHAREST
Heavy trading in first-tier stocks Azomures SA
fertiliser maker and chemical plant Oltchim SA, which joined
the market on Tuesday, kept turnover on the Bucharest bourse
high this week.
Demand outrunning supply sent the bulk of prices up on
Thursday, when two independent indices climbed to year highs.
Two unofficial VAB and BIG indices hit year highs.
TIRANA
For the second consecutive week, neither T-bills nor bonds
were traded on the dormant Tirana Stock Exchange during its two
weekly sessions on Monday and Thursday.
"Two banks are really taking care to preserve their
liquidity now since the lek is weakening," said a trade.
The local currency has hit a record low of about 130 leks
to the dollar, having plunged some 25 percent since the start
of the year as Albania plunged into its biggest political and
financial crisis since the fall of communism six years ago.
The collapse of several fraudulent investment schemes in
January left many Albanian penniless and has stirred weeks of
popular unrest across the country.
The right-wing government of President Sali Berisha has
promised help to some of the hardest-hit investors, but has
insisted that it will not print money to bail them out.
